news.author: Reuters
news.article_content:
The Trump administration plans to press ahead with efforts to block imports of Chinese data center equipment despite pushback from Amazon, Google, Meta and other US technology companies, people briefed on the matter said.

Reuters reported in August that the Federal Communications Commission was seeking to ban US imports of new models of Chinese optical transceivers, which allow data to travel over fiber-optic cables at the speed of light within data centers, over national security concerns. But the measure has faced more opposition than was previously known, with Amazon, Google, Meta , CoreWeave and Cisco joining Microsoft in a meeting with White House officials earlier this year. US firms could need up to a decade to comply with any such mandate, the executives told the officials, according to two people briefed on the meeting.

The lobbying had raised doubts over whether the measure would go ahead. But it is moving forward, three additional people familiar with the matter said, speaking on condition of anonymity because the deliberations are private. The push for stronger action comes as revelations about Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang’s affair with an alleged Chinese spy have fueled renewed calls in Washington for a tougher stance against Chinese technology threats.

China hawks in Washington are concerned Chinese transceivers could be used by Beijing to steal data, install malware or disrupt service at US data centers. The FCC, Amazon, Google, Meta, CoreWeave and Cisco did not respond to requests for comment. Microsoft declined to comment. A White House official declined to comment on the lobbying or the measure's progress but said recent FCC actions barring Chinese technology and other foreign equipment have resulted in billions in investments into US manufacturing, and thousands of new American jobs.

CHINA DOMINANT China boasts two-thirds of the global market for optical transceivers, according to Counterpoint Research. Chinese firms like Eoptolink (300502.SZ) and Zhongji Innolight (300308.SZ), which was added to the Pentagon's list of Chinese military-backed companies, dominate global supply, counting top American hyperscalers among their customers.

US-based Coherent (COHR.N) and Lumentum (LITE.O) produce technology that competes with them but lack the scale to replace Chinese vendors, according to a report by the Foundation for American Innovation. One of the people said the US firms raised the prospect of retaliation from China, in the form of a ban on the export of indium phosphide, a critical mineral needed for US firms to produce their own optical transceivers.

Trump has taken a more dovish approach to China in his second term, as he faces down Beijing's export controls on rare-earth minerals, which underpin tech manufacturing everywhere. But the FCC has been a notable exception, successfully barring imports of new models of Chinese drones, robots, power inverters and routers over the last year.

The Huang revelations have added to the pressure on the administration by turning a spotlight on cases of Nvidia AI chips being smuggled to China that went unaddressed by the Commerce Department.

(This story has not been edited by Devdiscourse staff and is auto-generated from a syndicated feed.)

news.article_content_zh:
尽管遭到亚马逊、谷歌、Meta 和其他美国科技公司的抵制，特朗普政府仍计划继续努力阻止进口中国数据中心设备。

路透社8月份报道称，出于国家安全考虑，美国联邦通信委员会正寻求禁止美国进口新型中国光收发器，这些光收发器允许数据在数据中心内以光速通过光纤电缆传输。但这项措施面临的反对比之前所知的要多，亚马逊、谷歌、Meta、CoreWeave 和思科今年早些时候与微软一起与白宫官员会面。据两位了解会议情况的人士透露，高管们告诉官员，美国公司可能需要长达十年的时间才能遵守此类指令。

游说活动引发了人们对该措施是否会继续实施的怀疑。但另外三名知情人士表示，该计划正在向前推进。由于讨论是私下进行的，因此要求匿名。在推动采取更强有力行动之际，英伟达首席执行官黄仁勋与一名涉嫌中国间谍的恋情被曝光，促使华盛顿再次呼吁对中国技术威胁采取更强硬的立场。

华盛顿的对华鹰派担心中国的收发器可能被北京用来窃取数据、安装恶意软件或破坏美国数据中心的服务。 FCC、亚马逊、谷歌、Meta、CoreWeave 和思科均未回应置评请求。微软拒绝置评。一位白宫官员拒绝就游说或该措施的进展发表评论，但表示，联邦通信委员会最近禁止中国技术和其他外国设备的行动已为美国制造业带来了数十亿美元的投资，并为美国创造了数千个新就业机会。

据 Counterpoint Research 称，中国占据全球光收发器市场三分之二的份额。新易盛科技（300502.SZ）和中际旭创（300308.SZ）等中国公司已被列入五角大楼的中国军方支持公司名单，它们在全球供应中占据主导地位，其客户中也包括美国顶级超大规模企业。

美国创新基金会的一份报告称，美国相干公司 (COHR.N) 和 Lumentum (LITE.O) 生产的技术可与它们竞争，但缺乏取代中国供应商的规模。其中一位人士表示，美国公司提出了中国可能采取报复措施的可能性，即禁止出口磷化铟，磷化铟是美国公司生产自己的光收发器所需的一种重要矿物。

特朗普在第二个任期内对中国采取了更为温和的态度，因为他面临北京对稀土矿产的出口管制，而稀土矿产是世界各地科技制造业的基础。但美国联邦通信委员会是一个值得注意的例外，去年成功禁止进口新型号的中国无人机、机器人、逆变器和路由器。

黄仁勋的爆料让英伟达人工智能芯片走私到中国的案件成为人们关注的焦点，而商务部却没有解决这一问题，这增加了政府的压力。

news.author: New York Times
news.article_content:
Tedious. Mind-numbing. Soul-destroying.

Ask visual-effects artists in Hollywood and most will agree: The task known as rotoscoping, while essential, is no fun.

Perhaps that is why an industry that has at times had its pitchforks out for everything artificial intelligence seems open to the idea that the technology can alleviate this particular burden.

Rotoscoping — even the name is insipid — involves methodically tracing around an object or a person, frame by frame and often for hours so that it can be isolated from the rest of the shot. A hologram of Princess Leia does not plead for help from Obi-Wan Kenobi in the original “Star Wars” (1977) without rotoscoping. Nor do the light sabers glow.

But can A.I. ease the drudgery? And can it do so with the same expert precision that human hands have provided for decades? What happens to those workers if their jobs get replaced?

More than a dozen people who work in visual effects in Hollywood acknowledged in interviews that some of the A.I.-powered rotoscoping tools they have begun to tinker with may be saving time and reducing tedium. But they stressed that the tools were far from perfect. Almost more important, they added, rotoscoping is a slice of moviemaking that offers valuable insight into how A.I. has begun to influence the industry.

“A.I. is not a simple conversation,” said Sang-Jin Bae, the director of the Martin Scorsese Virtual Production Center at New York University. But rotoscoping, he added, “is actually the perfect case study.”

Few viewers think about rotoscoping when watching a movie, but, as a foundational part of visual effects, it is indispensable.

Ever cut out a person from an image using Photoshop? “Roto,” as some call it, is like that but way more complicated and time-consuming. As characters and objects move through the frames of a film, each frame must be rotoed again to match the movements.

In many cases, rotoing requires breaking an object into sections and drawing shapes for each section. All those shapes must be repositioned to track the object’s progression across each frame.

“If you have an actor with long blond hair, and they’re flipping in the air fighting a robot, you need to roto every single hair,” said Jason Gottlieb, a longtime visual effects artist. “It’s the worst.”

Perhaps that is why rotoscoping often falls to entry-level employees. Marti Romances, a founder and the creative director of Territory Studio, recalled doing it 20 years ago.

“I wish back then, that instead of spending the first two years of my career doing these tedious things, I could have done other things that would teach me more about creativity,” he said.

Because all shots are different, experts hesitate to generalize about the costs and time involved in rotoscoping.

By some estimates, a person might spend a week rotoscoping a complicated five-second shot. Roto for an intricate one-minute scene could cost as much as $75,000.

Varying forms of machine learning have, in fact, been assisting with the most painstaking parts of moviemaking for several years, before so many advancements were grouped under the umbrella term of A.I.

In “Dune: Part Two” (2024), a machine-learning tool was used to locate all the eyeballs of the Fremen people and color them a radiant blue. When “Dune: Part One” was made a few years earlier, that work was accomplished only through countless hours of manual rotoscoping.

news.article_content_zh:
乏味。令人心麻木。毁灭灵魂。

询问好莱坞的视觉效果艺术家，大多数人都会同意：动态观察的任务虽然很重要，但并不有趣。

或许这就是为什么这个时常热衷于人工智能的行业似乎对这项技术可以减轻这种特殊负担的想法持开放态度。

动态观察——即使这个名字很平淡——需要有条不紊地围绕一个物体或一个人，一帧一帧地进行追踪，通常需要几个小时，以便将其与镜头的其余部分隔离开来。在原版《星球大战》（1977 年）中，莱娅公主的全息图并未向欧比旺·克诺比求助，无需转描。光剑也不发光。

但人工智能可以吗？减轻苦差事？它能否以与人类双手几十年来所提供的同样的专家精度来做到这一点？如果这些工人的工作被取代，他们会怎样？

十多名在好莱坞从事视觉效果工作的人在采访中承认，他们已经开始修补的一些人工智能驱动的动态描画工具可能会节省时间并减少乏味。但他们强调，这些工具远非完美。他们补充说，更重要的是，动态观察是电影制作的一部分，它为了解人工智能如何工作提供了宝贵的见解。已开始对行业产生影响。

“人工智能不是一场简单的对话，”纽约大学马丁·斯科塞斯虚拟制作中心主任裴尚金 (Sang-Jin Bae) 说。但他补充说，动态观察“实际上是一个完美的案例研究。”

很少有观众在观看电影时会想到动态观察，但作为视觉效果的基础部分，它是不可或缺的。

你曾经使用 Photoshop 从图像中剪出人物吗？有些人称之为“Roto”，与此类似，但更复杂且耗时。当角色和物体在电影的帧中移动时，每个帧都必须再次旋转以匹配运动。

在许多情况下，旋转需要将对象分成多个部分并为每个部分绘制形状。所有这些形状都必须重新定位，以跟踪对象在每一帧中的进展。

“如果你有一个长着金色长发的演员，他们在空中翻转与机器人战斗，你需要旋转每根头发，”长期视觉效果艺术家 Jason Gottlieb 说。 “这是最糟糕的。”

也许这就是为什么动态观察经常落到初级员工身上的原因。 Territory Studio 的创始人兼创意总监 Marti Romances 回忆起 20 年前的经历。

“我当时希望，我可以做其他事情来教会我更多关于创造力的事情，而不是在职业生涯的前两年做这些乏味的事情，”他说。

由于所有镜头都是不同的，专家们不愿对动态描画所涉及的成本和时间进行概括。

news.title: Chinese records: Alice Huang's husband Kang Wei built a state-backed data center network in China, with proposed investments exceeding $9B between 2021 and 2024 (Lingling Wei/Wall Street Journal)
news.title_en: Chinese records: Alice Huang's husband Kang Wei built a state-backed data center network in China, with proposed investments exceeding $9B between 2021 and 2024 (Lingling Wei/Wall Street Journal)
news.author: Wall Street Journal
news.article_content:
China's push to strengthen its AI capabilities involved two separate efforts allegedly linked to Alice Huang and her husband, Kang Wei, according to a Wall Street Journal investigation. While Kang expanded a network of data centres backed by the Chinese government, Alice reportedly built a close, romantic relationship with Nvidia's then-CEO Jensen Huang. The report claims she also helped create a channel for accessing Nvidia's advanced computing chips, several of which Washington has sought to prevent from reaching China. Together, their activities allegedly supported China's ambition to gain an edge over the US in artificial intelligence.

Kang Wei's business interests in China grew into a major data-centre operation, with projects worth more than $9 billion proposed between 2021 and 2024, a review of Chinese public records by the Wall Street Journal found. These ventures had financial backing from government-linked investors and were promoted as part of China's plan to build more computing infrastructure. The findings offer a closer look at Kang's previously unreported involvement in China's AI expansion, at a time when the US is trying to limit China's access to advanced computing technology.

Alice Huang’s Husband Built a $9 Billion Data-Center Empire Backed by the Chinese State While Alice Huang secured access to Nvidia’s advanced AI chips, her husband was building a sprawling network of government-backed computing infrastructure across China. A new Wall Street Journal investigation by Lingling Wei reveals another dimension of the Nvidia–Megaspeed controversy: the extensive business network built by Alice Huang’s husband, Kang Wei, and its connections to China’s state-backed AI ambitions. According to Chinese securities filings and government announcements reviewed by the Journal, proposed investments tied to Kang’s data-center network exceeded $9 billion between 2021 and 2024, with backing from Chinese government entities. At the center of this network is Century Longteng, a company whose ownership structure reportedly includes a 10% stake held by a Shanghai government entity, 27% associated with Kang’s investment network, and 63% held by Shenzhen-listed Century Huatong. In 2022, Century Longteng signed a cooperation agreement with Huawei, the Chinese technology giant subject to U.S. export restrictions, covering cloud data centers, energy infrastructure, and computing capacity. Kang’s network subsequently pursued several massive projects: Wuhu, Anhui: A proposed $4.5 billion development featuring eight data-center buildings and approximately 24,000 server racks, with local government support for power and infrastructure. Liangshan, Sichuan: Another proposed data-center development valued at approximately $5 billion, launched in 2024. Shenzhen: Additional data-center involvement documented in corporate filings. These projects align with Beijing’s national East Data, West Computing initiative, designed to expand and redistribute computing capacity across China. Meanwhile, Alice Huang’s Singapore-based company, Megaspeed, became an Nvidia Cloud Partner in 2023, gaining preferential access to advanced AI chips. Alibaba was identified as a major customer. The Wall Street Journal previously reported that at least some Nvidia chips acquired by Megaspeed were shipped to China. Even more concerning, Kang and Alice reportedly pitched data-center projects in Shanghai and Southeast Asia to prospective investors while claiming they could brin...
news.content_snippet: Kang Wei developed the business while his wife was involved with Nvidia's then-CEO — Alice Huang and her husband, Kang Wei …
news.summary_en: An investigation reveals that Kang Wei, husband of Alice Huang, developed a sprawling network of data centers in China with over $9 billion in proposed investments (2021-2024), backed by state-linked entities. The report highlights potential bypasses of U.S. export restrictions regarding Nvidia's advanced computing chips through these government-supported infrastructures.
news.article_content_en:
China's push to strengthen its AI capabilities involved two separate efforts allegedly linked to Alice Huang and her husband, Kang Wei, according to a Wall Street Journal investigation. While Kang expanded a network of data centres backed by the Chinese government, Alice reportedly built a close, romantic relationship with Nvidia's then-CEO Jensen Huang. The report claims she also helped create a channel for accessing Nvidia's advanced computing chips, several of which Washington has sought to prevent from reaching China. Together, their activities allegedly supported China's ambition to gain an edge over the US in artificial intelligence.

Kang Wei's business interests in China grew into a major data-centre operation, with projects worth more than $9 billion proposed between 2021 and 2024, a review of Chinese public records by the Wall Street Journal found. These ventures had financial backing from government-linked investors and were promoted as part of China's plan to build more computing infrastructure. The findings offer a closer look at Kang's previously unreported involvement in China's AI expansion, at a time when the US is trying to limit China's access to advanced computing technology.

Alice Huang’s Husband Built a $9 Billion Data-Center Empire Backed by the Chinese State While Alice Huang secured access to Nvidia’s advanced AI chips, her husband was building a sprawling network of government-backed computing infrastructure across China. A new Wall Street Journal investigation by Lingling Wei reveals another dimension of the Nvidia–Megaspeed controversy: the extensive business network built by Alice Huang’s husband, Kang Wei, and its connections to China’s state-backed AI ambitions. According to Chinese securities filings and government announcements reviewed by the Journal, proposed investments tied to Kang’s data-center network exceeded $9 billion between 2021 and 2024, with backing from Chinese government entities. At the center of this network is Century Longteng, a company whose ownership structure reportedly includes a 10% stake held by a Shanghai government entity, 27% associated with Kang’s investment network, and 63% held by Shenzhen-listed Century Huatong. In 2022, Century Longteng signed a cooperation agreement with Huawei, the Chinese technology giant subject to U.S. export restrictions, covering cloud data centers, energy infrastructure, and computing capacity. Kang’s network subsequently pursued several massive projects: Wuhu, Anhui: A proposed $4.5 billion development featuring eight data-center buildings and approximately 24,000 server racks, with local government support for power and infrastructure. Liangshan, Sichuan: Another proposed data-center development valued at approximately $5 billion, launched in 2024. Shenzhen: Additional data-center involvement documented in corporate filings. These projects align with Beijing’s national East Data, West Computing initiative, designed to expand and redistribute computing capacity across China. Meanwhile, Alice Huang’s Singapore-based company, Megaspeed, became an Nvidia Cloud Partner in 2023, gaining preferential access to advanced AI chips. Alibaba was identified as a major customer. The Wall Street Journal previously reported that at least some Nvidia chips acquired by Megaspeed were shipped to China. Even more concerning, Kang and Alice reportedly pitched data-center projects in Shanghai and Southeast Asia to prospective investors while claiming they could bring Nvidia chips into China. This raises a much bigger question than Jensen Huang’s personal relationship with Alice Huang. How did access to America’s most advanced AI hardware intersect with a multibillion-dollar computing infrastructure network backed by the Chinese state? Importantly, the Journal acknowledges that the available public records do not establish that Beijing directed Megaspeed’s chip purchases or that those chips ultimately reached Kang’s data centers. Those connections remain unproven and require further investigation. But the broader national security implications are impossible to ignore. While Washington was trying to restrict China’s access to advanced AI computing power, one couple was operating on both sides of the technological divide: One had a privileged procurement channel into Nvidia’s chip ecosystem and a personal relationship with its then-CEO. The other was developing billions of dollars’ worth of computing infrastructure with Chinese government backing. How did this arrangement develop, who knew about it, and what safeguards were in place to prevent American technology from strengthening China’s military and strategic AI capabilities? This is no longer just a story about a CEO’s romantic scandal. It is a story about export controls, corporate accountability, and the potential intersection of American technological leadership with China’s state-backed AI ambitions. And it demands answers. https://t.co/iImQYdKQFJ

Kang's entry into the sector began in 2021 through Century Longteng, a Shanghai-based company backed by both private investors and a local government body. He later joined its leadership and helped steer its expansion into data centres. One of its early major partnerships was with Huawei in 2022, covering cloud computing, energy systems and data-centre infrastructure. The company then announced plans for a massive computing park in Wuhu, with an estimated investment of $4.5 billion. The development was designed to include eight buildings and space for roughly 24,000 server racks. A separate project worth around $5 billion was announced in Sichuan in 2024.

As Kang pursued data-centre projects in China, his wife Alice Huang was working on a separate business front involving Nvidia chips. Her company, Megaspeed, reportedly told Nvidia in November 2023 that Alibaba would be a major customer. It subsequently received cloud partner status, which offered it priority access to Nvidia processors. The WSJ has reported that some of the chips obtained by Megaspeed were later sent to China. However, there is no public evidence establishing that the Chinese government directed these purchases or that the processors were used in Kang's data centres. Alice was also reportedly in a romantic relationship with Nvidia's then-CEO Jensen Huang, whom Kang had known since their time in the video game industry.

The couple's business activities have since come under scrutiny. Singapore began investigating Megaspeed and several individuals in February 2025 over suspected false declarations related to server purchases. While authorities said there was not enough evidence to establish domestic criminal offences, Alice received a formal warning and was barred from entering Singapore. The investigation involving Megaspeed and six other people is still ongoing. Separately, Kang was detained in Shanghai earlier this year in connection with a stock-market manipulation inquiry, according to the WSJ, but has since been released. Megaspeed has defended its operations as legitimate and lawful and said Alice no longer works with the company.

news.article_content_zh:
康在中国政府的支持下扩大了数据中心网络，而爱丽丝则与英伟达时任首席执行官黄仁勋建立了密切的浪漫关系。该报告称，她还帮助创建了一个获取英伟达先进计算芯片的渠道，华盛顿一直试图阻止其中一些芯片进入中国。据称，他们的活动共同支持了中国在人工智能领域超越美国的雄心。

《华尔街日报》对中国公共记录的审查发现，康伟在中国的商业利益已发展成为一项重要的数据中心业务，在 2021 年至 2024 年间提出的项目价值超过 90 亿美元。这些企业得到了与政府相关的投资者的财政支持，并作为中国建设更多计算基础设施计划的一部分得到推广。在美国试图限制中国获得先进计算技术之际，这些调查结果让我们更仔细地了解了康此前未报道的参与中国人工智能扩张的情况。

Alice Huang 的丈夫在中国政府的支持下建立了价值 90 亿美元的数据中心帝国 虽然 Alice Huang 获得了 Nvidia 先进人工智能芯片的使用权，但她的丈夫正在中国各地建立一个由政府支持的计算基础设施组成的庞大网络。 《华尔街日报》由 Lingling Wei 进行的一项新调查揭示了 Nvidia 与 Megaspeed 争议的另一个方面：Alice Huang 的丈夫 Kang Wei 建立的广泛商业网络及其与中国国家支持的人工智能雄心的联系。根据《华尔街日报》查阅的中国证券备案文件和政府公告，在中国政府实体的支持下，2021 年至 2024 年间与康的数据中心网络相关的拟议投资超过 90 亿美元。该网络的核心是世纪龙腾，据报道，该公司的股权结构包括上海一家政府实体持有 10% 的股份，康氏投资网络持有 27% 的股份，深圳上市公司世纪华通持有 63% 的股份。 2022年，世纪龙腾与受美国出口限制的中国科技巨头华为签署合作协议，涵盖云数据中心、能源基础设施、计算能力等领域。康的网络随后开展了几个大型项目： 安徽芜湖：拟议耗资 45 亿美元的开发项目，包括八座数据中心大楼和约 24,000 个服务器机架，并得到当地政府对电力和基础设施的支持。四川凉山：另一个拟议的数据中心开发项目价值约 50 亿美元，将于 2024 年启动。深圳：公司备案中记录了更多数据中心参与情况。这些项目与北京国家“东数据、西计算”倡议相一致，旨在扩大和重新分配中国各地的计算能力。与此同时，Alice Huang 的新加坡公司 Megaspeed 于 2023 年成为 Nvidia 云合作伙伴，获得了先进人工智能芯片的优先使用权。阿里巴巴被认定为主要客户。 《华尔街日报》此前报道称，Megaspeed 收购的至少部分 Nvidia 芯片被运往中国。更令人担忧的是，据报道，康和爱丽丝向潜在投资者推销上海和东南亚的数据中心项目，同时声称他们可以将英伟达芯片引入中国。这提出了一个比黄仁勋与黄爱丽丝的个人关系更大的问题。美国最先进的人工智能硬件如何与中国政府支持的价值数十亿美元的计算基础设施网络相结合？重要的是，《华尔街日报》承认，现有的公共记录并不能证明北京指导了 Megaspeed 的芯片采购，也不能证明这些芯片最终到达了康的数据中心。这些联系尚未得到证实，需要进一步调查。但更广泛的国家安全影响不容忽视。当华盛顿试图限制中国获得先进的人工智能计算能力时，一对夫妇在技术鸿沟的两边进行操作：其中一方拥有进入英伟达芯片生态系统的特权采购渠道，并与其时任首席执行官有私人关系。另一个是在中国政府的支持下开发价值数十亿美元的计算基础设施。这种安排是如何发展的，谁知道这一点，以及采取了哪些保障措施来防止美国技术加强中国的军事和战略人工智能能力？这不再只是一个关于首席执行官的浪漫丑闻的故事。这是一个关于出口管制、企业责任以及美国技术领先地位与中国国家支持的人工智能雄心的潜在交集的故事。它需要答案。

康于 2021 年通过世纪龙腾进入该行业，这是一家总部位于上海的公司，得到了私人投资者和地方政府机构的支持。后来他加入了该公司的领导层，并帮助引导该公司向数据中心扩张。其早期的主要合作伙伴之一是 2022 年与华为建立的合作伙伴关系，涵盖云计算、能源系统和数据中心基础设施。该公司随后宣布计划在芜湖建设一个大型计算园区，预计投资 45 亿美元。该开发项目包括八栋建筑和可容纳约 24,000 个服务器机架的空间。 2024 年，四川宣布了一个价值约 50 亿美元的单独项目。

当康在中国开展数据中心项目时，他的妻子爱丽丝·黄 (Alice Huang) 正在从事涉及 Nvidia 芯片的独立业务。据报道，她的公司 Megaspeed 在 2023 年 11 月告诉 Nvidia，阿里巴巴将成为其主要客户。随后它获得了云合作伙伴地位，这使其能够优先使用 Nvidia 处理器。据《华尔街日报》报道，Megaspeed 获得的部分芯片后来被运往中国。然而，没有公开证据证明中国政府指导了这些采购，或者这些处理器被用于康的数据中心。据报道，爱丽丝还与英伟达时任首席执行官黄仁勋保持着恋爱关系，康从电子游戏行业就认识了黄仁勋。

此后，这对夫妇的商业活动受到密切关注。新加坡于 2025 年 2 月开始调查 Megaspeed 和数名个人涉嫌与服务器购买相关的虚假声明。虽然当局表示没有足够的证据证明她犯有国内刑事犯罪，但爱丽丝还是收到了正式警告...

news.article_content:
Then I remembered: Wait, I can ask Siri to remind me! At a traffic light, I double-tapped the digital crown on the Apple Watch, and Siri's new Live Rewind feature spun back the clock 15 seconds and showed me a transcript of what my wife said.

I sheepishly interrupted her to show her the transcript. “Look!” Her reply? “Why wouldn't you just ask me to repeat myself?” She shrugged at this new Apple Watch capability and continued talking.

A few days later, I was chatting with my brother on my stoop. Once again, I lost focus for a few seconds and remembered to ask Siri to help me recall what my brother said moments ago. But this time, before I excitedly showed my brother the Apple Watch screen, I preemptively said, “Yeah, I know I could just ask you to repeat yourself.” I got a perplexed look back.

Live Rewind, one of Apple's new Audio Intelligence features on its latest Apple Watches, is designed to give you a transcript of the last 15 seconds of a conversation. It's in public beta in watchOS 27.3, but is expected to launch officially before the year's end.

Coming alongside it is another new capability called Siri Recap: Give the assistant permission to listen to your environment—you can set schedules or have it trigger when you reach the office—and you'll see a “Recap” in the Siri app at the end of the day. It’ll show you summaries of conversations and list out important details that people said. It's very similar to AI notetakers, many of which run on dedicated hardware devices.

The power here is that it all happens on your Apple Watch, the same device you wear everywhere to track your fitness, monitor health, and check notifications. That ubiquity is exactly what makes privacy advocates uneasy—they say features like these normalize ambient surveillance, much like smart glasses, undermining the privacy of bystanders who don't consent to being recorded.

“One of the concerns that we have with things like the Apple Watch is we don't know what the watch is picking up on,” Reem Suleiman, senior campaign director at the nonprofit digital rights advocacy group Fight for the Future, tells WIRED. “Just because the device wearer is the one opting in to use the feature, you're not getting consent from everybody who you walk around.”

in, and they are limited to the latest Apple Watch Series 12 or Apple Watch Ultra 4. They also require an iPhone 16 or newer with iOS 27 and Apple Intelligence. These features are not available for users under 18, and they currently work only in English.

For Live Rewind, the audio is processed on-device and cannot be accessed. When you activate it, a small chime plays from the Apple Watch that serves as a warning for folks nearby. Text disappears unless you choose to save it to Siri. For Recaps, Siri keeps them factual, doesn't identify speakers, and also omits content the system deems sensitive. If you don't save a Recap, it'll self-delete in seven days. Apple uses its Private Cloud Compute processing system for the data, which is never stored or logged on its servers. Data stored in the Siri app is end-to-end encrypted when syncing with iCloud.

Even if you're happy with Apple's privacy focus, I haven't found these capabilities tremendously useful over the past week. Live Rewind works well in moderately quiet environments, but the transcript can quickly turn into inaccurate gibberish when there's a lot of background noise.

news.article_content_zh:
然后我想起来：等等，我可以让 Siri 提醒我！在红绿灯处，我双击了 Apple Watch 上的数字表冠，Siri 的新实时倒带功能将时钟倒转 15 秒，并向我展示了我妻子所说的话的文字记录。

我不好意思地打断她，给她看成绩单。 “看！”她的答复？ “你为什么不让我重复一遍呢？”她对 Apple Watch 的新功能耸了耸肩，然后继续说话。

几天后，我在门廊上和弟弟聊天。我再次失去注意力几秒钟，然后记得让 Siri 帮我回忆一下我哥哥刚才说的话。但这一次，在我兴奋地向弟弟展示 Apple Watch 屏幕之前，我先发制人地说：“是的，我知道我可以请你重复一遍。”我回头看了一眼，感到很困惑。

Live Rewind 是 Apple 在最新款 Apple Watch 上新增的音频智能功能之一，旨在为您提供最后 15 秒对话的记录。它在 watchOS 27.3 中处于公开测试版，但预计将在年底前正式发布。

与此同时，还有另一项名为 Siri Recap 的新功能：允许助理聆听您的环境，您可以设置时间表或在到达办公室时触发它，然后您会在一天结束时在 Siri 应用程序中看到“Recap”。它会向您显示对话摘要并列出人们所说的重要细节。它与人工智能记事本非常相似，其中许多记事本都在专用硬件设备上运行。

这里的强大之处在于，这一切都发生在您的 Apple Watch 上，您在任何地方都佩戴这款设备来跟踪您的健身情况、监控健康状况和检查通知。这种无处不在的现象正是让隐私倡导者感到不安的原因——他们表示，此类功能使环境监控正常化，就像智能​​眼镜一样，破坏了不同意被记录的旁观者的隐私。

非营利性数字版权倡导组织“为未来而战”的高级活动总监雷姆·苏莱曼 (Reem Suleiman) 告诉《连线》杂志：“我们对 Apple Watch 等产品的担忧之一是我们不知道这款手表能接收到什么信息。” “仅仅因为设备佩戴者是选择使用该功能的人，你就不会得到你周围的每个人的同意。”

苹果花费了大量精力来解释该系统的工作原理以及该公司计划如何维护用户及其周围人的隐私。首先，这些功能是可选的，并且仅限于最新的 Apple Watch Series 12 或 Apple Watch Ultra 4。它们还需要配备 iOS 27 和 Apple Intelligence 的 iPhone 16 或更新版本。这些功能不适用于 18 岁以下的用户，并且目前仅支持英语。

对于实时倒带，音频在设备上进行处理并且无法访问。当你激活它时，Apple Watch 会发出一声小铃声，向附近的人发出警告。除非您选择将其保存到 Siri，否则文本会消失。对于 Recaps，Siri 会保持事实性，不会识别发言者，还会忽略系统认为敏感的内容。如果您不保存回顾，它将在 7 天内自行删除。苹果使用其私有云计算处理系统来处理数据，这些数据永远不会存储或记录在其服务器上。与 iCloud 同步时，Siri 应用程序中存储的数据会进行端到端加密。

即使您对苹果公司对隐私的关注感到满意，但在过去的一周里我并没有发现这些功能非常有用。实时倒带在适度安静的环境中效果很好，但当背景噪音很大时，文字记录很快就会变成不准确的乱码。

在与你聊天的人面前激活它会让人感觉很尴尬。这就像有人试图与你交谈时掏出你的智能手机一样——有点粗鲁和分散注意力。您不是将屏幕放在视线之外（数字排毒的一大趋势），而是在人类对话中引入屏幕。我再次向妻子提起这个话题，她也表达了其中的一些感受，说这感觉像是一个会阻碍一个人社交技能的功能。他们没有要求别人重复一遍，而是将 Apple Watch 加入其中来填补空白。

我并不是说这没有帮助。当它发挥作用时，感觉就像拥有超能力。也许在某些情况下，您不想打断小组对话并要求某人重复一遍。不过，现在存在的问题是记住这个功能的存在并记住使用它。我还发现 15 秒规则有点太短，导致我错过了部分对话。

回顾一下更有帮助一些。出于测试目的，我已将 Siri 设置为每天全天进行回顾，但我喜欢您可以创建自定义时间表或在到达特定位置（例如办公室）时触发它。您可以在 Apple Watch 的控制中心中手动打开或关闭 Siri Recap。最令人印象深刻的是，尽管不断启用 Recap，但我没有看到电池寿命出现明显下降。一天半后，我继续为 Apple Watch Series 12 充电。

更令人困惑的事情之一是打开 Siri 应用程序查看我的回顾，并发现一堆我不记得的对话。事实证明，Siri 正在录制我正在观看的媒体，例如 YouTube 或 Instagram 上的媒体。这是我在使用人工智能记事本时遇到的一个问题，比如亚马逊旗下的 Bee AI 可穿戴设备，它声称正在致力于“活体检测”来解决这个问题。其最新的硬件附带了一项功能，如果在设定的时间内未检测到佩戴者的声音，则不会记录对话。希望苹果能够找到解决方案。目前，您可以编辑或删除这些摘要。

news.author: Wired AI
news.article_content:
As the agents worked at superhuman speed to probe and exploit systems, Hugging Face confronted a bewildering deluge of data. The company’s engineers were only able to analyze the attack by using an open-weight model called GLM 5.2 from a Chinese company called Z.ai.

Delangue moved to the US more than a decade ago, “barely speaking English,” and built Hugging Face into a platform that supports tens of millions of AI developers. The fresh-faced Frenchman, who dresses even more like a skater than most AI execs, says the summer attack highlighted the value of open-weight models, which unlike ChatGPT or Claude can be downloaded and run by anyone.

Despite championing the democratization of AI, however, Hugging Face was acquired by one of the industry’s biggest players, Nvidia, for $12.93 billion in September. When I caught up with Delangue recently, that was the subject of my first question.

This interview has been edited for length and clarity.

CLÉMENT DELANGUE: We need more resources to give open-source AI a chance. It has grown really well in the past few years and has become a really credible alternative to closed-source APIs. But the field is still dominated by closed-source.

We’re gonna have the Anthropic IPO in a few weeks. They basically went from zero to a top five or top 10 most valuable company in the world in a few years. I don't think that's ever happened before.

Does Anthropic's IPO suggest the closed approach is winning?

It’s hard to say. I've always said that there is a very strong natural tendency for AI to concentrate capabilities and wealth. People haven't internalized how much of the future compute capacity has already been reserved by a few companies. Talent, compute, resources—these all fuel the natural tendency for AI to be dominated by a few closed-source labs.

Let’s talk about the attack. When did you first realize Hugging Face was being hacked by a group of AI agents?

At the beginning, it didn't go to the top of our priority list. It just wasn't bad enough to really trigger that. The goal was pretty narrow and wasn’t deemed to be very dangerous or damaging. But it was raising questions. Especially the number of actions taken compared to the narrowness of the goal. It was surprising to us, and we couldn't really fit it into a familiar pattern. That's why we started investigating.

And you used the Chinese model called GLM to investigate.

I actually think that 95 percent of the risks are being created by a few companies that are pushing the frontier behind closed doors. And 95 percent of the protection or defense is going to be done by the open-source ecosystem.

Does the US need its own open-weight models—ones as powerful as GLM, DeepSeek, Kimi, or Qwen?

Yeah, I think it's very, very important for sovereignty, for understanding AI, and for academia. It’s kind of weird that most academic labs have to use Chinese models because they’re the ones that are open. If you go to Stanford or MIT, you have no choice but to use the Chinese open-weight models.

There is some momentum, but I don't think it's enough. I think there's a lot more to do. A lot more investment is needed.

The best open-source non-Chinese models are actually coming from outside of the US. Right from France, Mistral; Cohere from Canada; South Korea is starting to do more and more. But it’s still pretty far from what the US could do.

news.article_content_zh:
当特工们以超人的速度探测和利用系统时，Hugging Face 面临着令人眼花缭乱的海量数据。该公司的工程师只能使用中国 Z.ai 公司的 GLM 5.2 开放权重模型来分析攻击。

Delangue 十多年前移居美国，“几乎不会说英语”，并将 Hugging Face 打造成一个支持数千万人工智能开发者的平台。这位面容新鲜的法国人比大多数人工智能高管穿得更像一名滑冰运动员，他表示，夏季袭击凸显了开放重量模型的价值，与 ChatGPT 或 Claude 不同，任何人都可以下载和运行该模型。

尽管倡导人工智能的民主化，Hugging Face 还是在 9 月份被业界最大的公司之一英伟达 (Nvidia) 以 129.3 亿美元的价格收购。当我最近采访德兰格时，这是我第一个问题的主题。

为了篇幅和清晰度，本次采访经过编辑。

CLÉMENT DELANGUE：我们需要更多资源来为开源人工智能提供机会。它在过去几年中发展得非常好，并且已经成为闭源 API 的真正可靠的替代品。但该领域仍然以闭源为主。

几周后我们将进行 Anthropic 首次公开募股。他们基本上在几年内从零跻身全球最有价值公司前五名或前十名。我认为以前从未发生过这种情况。

Anthropic 的 IPO 是否表明封闭式方法正在获胜？

很难说。我一直说，人工智能有一种非常强烈的自然倾向，即集中能力和财富。人们还没有意识到未来的计算能力有多少已经被一些公司保留了。人才、计算、资源——这些都助长了人工智能由少数闭源实验室主导的自然趋势。

我们来谈谈攻击。您什么时候第一次意识到 Hugging Face 被一群人工智能 智能体黑客攻击？

一开始，它并没有成为我们优先考虑的事项。只是还没有糟糕到真正触发这一点。这个目标相当狭窄，并不被认为是非常危险或具有破坏​​性的。但这引发了疑问。尤其是与目标的狭窄程度相比，所采取的行动的数量。这让我们感到惊讶，而且我们无法真正将其融入到熟悉的模式中。这就是我们开始调查的原因。

你们使用了中国的模型 GLM 来进行调查。

事实上，我认为 95% 的风险是由少数几家闭门推进前沿的公司造成的。 95% 的保护或防御将由开源生态系统完成。

美国是否需要自己的开放权重模型——像 GLM、DeepSeek、Kimi 或 Qwen 这样强大的模型？

是的，我认为这对于主权、理解人工智能和学术界都非常非常重要。奇怪的是，大多数学术实验室都必须使用中国模型，因为它们是开放的。如果你去斯坦福或者麻省理工，你别无选择，只能使用中国的开放权重模型。

news.title: A look at Anthropic's data center network plans, dubbed Anthropic Direct, committing $900B+ through 2045; docs show it will lease 875K TPUs for $7.2B per year (Financial Times)
news.title_en: A look at Anthropic's data center network plans, dubbed Anthropic Direct, committing $900B+ through 2045; docs show it will lease 875K TPUs for $7.2B per year (Financial Times)
news.author: Financial Times
news.article_content:
Anthropic is cutting out the cloud middleman and moving to become a major direct player in the data center market, with plans to lease dedicated data centers at significant scale as the company’s computing needs surge in advance of its highly anticipated public offering.

The shift was disclosed Monday in the Claude maker's S-1 filing that sparked reports of a possibly record-setting IPO and marks a significant strategic change for Anthropic. The company has relied almost entirely on cloud providers like Amazon, Google and Microsoft for its computing power.

But under an initiative the company is calling Anthropic Direct, leased data centers under Anthropic’s control will account for a growing share of the $542B to $567B the company plans to spend on computing infrastructure in the coming years.

Wikimedia Commons/TechCrunch Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei in 2023While the move comes with a significant set of risks, it will also immediately establish Anthropic as one of the digital infrastructure ecosystem’s largest drivers of demand for data center capacity.

"As our compute requirements have scaled, we have transitioned to a hybrid model in which, in addition to purchasing compute as a cloud service, we also procure specialized AI accelerators directly and operate this hardware in dedicated data center facilities leased and operated on our behalf, to our specification," the company wrote in its SEC filing.

Anthropic Direct will not see the company build its own data centers. Rather, Anthropic plans to rely on third-party providers to secure sites and power, build facilities to its specifications and manage them on an ongoing basis, a model often used by hyperscalers.

The initiative is already moving beyond the planning stage, with Anthropic recently entering into purchase and lease agreements for Anthropic Direct, according to its SEC filing.

While this will be Anthropic’s first time pursuing large-scale data center tenancy, the company has been integral to data center development deals in the past. Last November, Anthropic announced a $50B infrastructure investment through which neocloud Fluidstack would develop data centers in Texas and New York to provide the company with computing capacity. Anthropic Direct represents a step further in controlling the physical infrastructure underpinning its artificial intelligence models.

Until now, Anthropic has purchased nearly all its computing capacity as a service from outside cloud providers. The bulk of that capacity has come from Amazon, Google and Microsoft, while the company has signed smaller deals with SpaceX and a number of neoclouds, among them Fluidstack and Lambda. The firm’s S-1 filing offers new insight into the scale of these commitments: By the end of 2025, Anthropic inked $417B in compute deals with various providers.

Yet Anthropic itself identifies this dependence on cloud firms as a significant source of risk. The filing describes its relationship with the major cloud providers as “multifaceted and complex” because many of the same companies supplying Anthropic with compute are also direct competitors, operating AI labs and developing products that compete with Claude. These cloud providers, the filing says, could “prioritize their own computing needs” over Anthropic’s or “gain insight” into Anthropic’s infrastructure and computing requirements that “could inform their competitive strategies.”

news.article_content_en:
Anthropic is cutting out the cloud middleman and moving to become a major direct player in the data center market, with plans to lease dedicated data centers at significant scale as the company’s computing needs surge in advance of its highly anticipated public offering.

The shift was disclosed Monday in the Claude maker's S-1 filing that sparked reports of a possibly record-setting IPO and marks a significant strategic change for Anthropic. The company has relied almost entirely on cloud providers like Amazon, Google and Microsoft for its computing power.

But under an initiative the company is calling Anthropic Direct, leased data centers under Anthropic’s control will account for a growing share of the $542B to $567B the company plans to spend on computing infrastructure in the coming years.

Wikimedia Commons/TechCrunch Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei in 2023While the move comes with a significant set of risks, it will also immediately establish Anthropic as one of the digital infrastructure ecosystem’s largest drivers of demand for data center capacity.

"As our compute requirements have scaled, we have transitioned to a hybrid model in which, in addition to purchasing compute as a cloud service, we also procure specialized AI accelerators directly and operate this hardware in dedicated data center facilities leased and operated on our behalf, to our specification," the company wrote in its SEC filing.

Anthropic Direct will not see the company build its own data centers. Rather, Anthropic plans to rely on third-party providers to secure sites and power, build facilities to its specifications and manage them on an ongoing basis, a model often used by hyperscalers.

The initiative is already moving beyond the planning stage, with Anthropic recently entering into purchase and lease agreements for Anthropic Direct, according to its SEC filing.

While this will be Anthropic’s first time pursuing large-scale data center tenancy, the company has been integral to data center development deals in the past. Last November, Anthropic announced a $50B infrastructure investment through which neocloud Fluidstack would develop data centers in Texas and New York to provide the company with computing capacity. Anthropic Direct represents a step further in controlling the physical infrastructure underpinning its artificial intelligence models.

Until now, Anthropic has purchased nearly all its computing capacity as a service from outside cloud providers. The bulk of that capacity has come from Amazon, Google and Microsoft, while the company has signed smaller deals with SpaceX and a number of neoclouds, among them Fluidstack and Lambda. The firm’s S-1 filing offers new insight into the scale of these commitments: By the end of 2025, Anthropic inked $417B in compute deals with various providers.

Yet Anthropic itself identifies this dependence on cloud firms as a significant source of risk. The filing describes its relationship with the major cloud providers as “multifaceted and complex” because many of the same companies supplying Anthropic with compute are also direct competitors, operating AI labs and developing products that compete with Claude. These cloud providers, the filing says, could “prioritize their own computing needs” over Anthropic’s or “gain insight” into Anthropic’s infrastructure and computing requirements that “could inform their competitive strategies.”

Anthropic Direct reduces some of that dependence, but it also introduces a new set of risks identified in its S-1 filing. Leasing and deploying data center infrastructure directly requires more capital up front, potentially impacting the firm’s available liquidity. It also leaves Anthropic more directly exposed to the development risks facing the broader data center sector, particularly project delays from community opposition, supply chain constraints and power shortages.

“If we are unable to successfully execute on our data center infrastructure initiatives, experience significant delays or cost overruns, or find that the infrastructure we lease, deploy, or build does not meet our evolving needs, we may not realize the expected benefits of these investments, which could adversely affect our business, financial condition, and results of operation,” the filing says.

news.article_content_zh:
Anthropic 正在消除云中间商，成为数据中心市场的主要直接参与者，并计划大规模租赁专用数据中心，因为该公司的计算需求在其备受期待的公开发行之前激增。

这一转变在周一 Claude 制造商的 S-1 文件中披露，引发了有关可能创纪录的 IPO 的报道，并标志着 Anthropic 的重大战略变化。该公司几乎完全依赖亚马逊、谷歌和微软等云提供商的计算能力。

但根据该公司称为 Anthropic Direct 的一项计划，Anthropic 控制下的租赁数据中心将在该公司计划未来几年用于计算基础设施的 $542B 至 $567B 支出中占据越来越大的份额。

Wikimedia Commons/TechCrunch Anthropic 首席执行官 Dario Amodei 于 2023 年虽然此举会带来一系列重大风险，但它也将立即使 Anthropic 成为数字基础设施生态系统数据中心容量需求的最大驱动因素之一。

该公司在向 SEC 提交的文件中写道：“随着我们的计算需求不断扩大，我们已经转向混合模式，除了购买计算作为云服务外，我们还直接采购专门的人工智能加速器，并按照我们的规范在代表我们租赁和运营的专用数据中心设施中运行这些硬件。”

Anthropic Direct 不会看到该公司建立自己的数据中心。相反，Anthropic 计划依靠第三方提供商来保护站点和电力、按照其规格建造设施并持续管理它们，这是超大规模企业经常使用的模式。

根据向 SEC 提交的文件，该计划已经超出了规划阶段，Anthropic 最近签署了 Anthropic Direct 的购买和租赁协议。

虽然这将是 Anthropic 首次寻求大规模数据中心租赁，但该公司过去一直是数据中心开发交易中不可或缺的一部分。去年 11 月，Anthropic 宣布进行 500 亿美元的基础设施投资，neocloud Fluidstack 将通过该投资在德克萨斯州和纽约开发数据中心，为公司提供计算能力。 Anthropic Direct 代表着在控制支撑其人工智能模型的物理基础设施方面又向前迈出了一步。

到目前为止，Anthropic 已经从外部云提供商那里购买了几乎所有的计算能力作为服务。其中大部分容量来自亚马逊、谷歌和微软，而该公司还与 SpaceX 和一些 Neocloud 签署了较小的协议，其中包括 Fluidstack 和 Lambda。该公司的 S-1 文件提供了对这些承诺规模的新见解：到 2025 年底，Anthropic 与各种提供商签署了 417B 美元的计算协议。

然而，Anthropic 本身认为这种对云公司的依赖是一个重要的风险来源。该文件将其与主要云提供商的关系描述为“多方面且复杂”，因为许多为 Anthropic 提供计算的公司也是直接竞争对手，运营人工智能实验室并开发与 Claude 竞争的产品。文件称，这些云提供商可以“优先考虑自己的计算需求”而不是 Anthropic 的需求，或者“深入了解”Anthropic 的基础设施和计算需求，“可以为他们的竞争策略提供信息”。

Anthropic Direct 在一定程度上减少了这种依赖性，但也引入了 S-1 文件中确定的一系列新风险。租赁和部署数据中心基础设施直接需要更多的前期资本，可能会影响公司的可用流动性。这也使得 Anthropic 更直接地面临更广泛的数据中心行业面临的发展风险，特别是社区反对、供应链限制和电力短缺造成的项目延误。

文件称：“如果我们无法成功执行我们的数据中心基础设施计划，经历严重的延误或成本超支，或者发现我们租赁、部署或建造的基础设施不能满足我们不断变化的需求，我们可能无法实现这些投资的预期效益，这可能会对我们的业务、财务状况和运营业绩产生不利影响。”

news.article_content:
Steelberg, alongside fellow Google alumnus and former Apple executive Andy Baynes, says they are trying to break the Russia-Ukraine war “stalemate,” Silicon Valley–style. They believe their experience building and iterating technology quickly can help bring Western weapon manufacturing in line with the rapid innovation cycles seen on the battlefield and beat the “attritional cat-and-mouse technology game” that the war, as Baynes describes it, has become.

Steelberg, originally from Newport Beach, California, started itching to “make a difference” on the battlefield after he took in a couple hundred Ukrainian refugees into his French chateau in early 2022. He says he was regularly “heartbroken” by the outpouring of grief whenever bad news arrived about a husband, father, or son back home. “I believe I could really change the outcome of this and every war,” Steelberg tells WIRED. "I'm not saying this is purely altruistic,” he adds. “Of course we're going to be making money doing it."

This week, their firm, Tiberius Aerospace, said it had secured $85 million in Series A financing, led by European technology investment firm Lakestar and Rochefort Asset Management, a national-security-focused investment firm licensed under the US Defense Department. Ukrainian venture capital firm UA1 is also an investor.

Tiberius began as Steelberg’s private research lab, incorporated in 2021, which employed people across France, the UK, and US to experiment on left-field ideas across a range of technologies, from drones and electric vertical takeoff aircraft to quantum computing. After the invasion, he pivoted the lab’s AI and aerospace engineers into writing code and building spreadsheets to objectively analyze the war’s many factors and calculate what could move the needle. The AI model they created quickly ruled out building better defensive technology because that would just harden the stalemate.

With his aim narrowed to building an offensive weapon, Steelberg developed several metrics to numerically analyze the lethality of different systems, including cost-effectiveness, and used the AI engine to simulate weapons under different conditions and identify what would disrupt the market. Don’t build another drone, it suggested, build longer-range artillery munitions. The resulting system, called Sceptre, can be fired from a 155-millimeter howitzer—the most common artillery weapon donated to Ukraine. As well as traveling farther than currently available rounds, they claim they can reach supersonic speeds and altitudes beyond jamming range.

Giving Ukraine’s guns extra range is important, Sam Cranny-Evans, an associate fellow at UK defense think tank the Royal United Services Institute, tells WIRED, because it would allow Ukrainian gunners to operate beyond the reach of Russian drone attacks. 155-mm shells “can cause massive damage to a group of vehicles or infantry,” he says. “Any technology that can help Ukraine extend the reach of its howitzers and return them to combat would be valuable.”

With a prototype he’d designed with the help of AI, Steelberg also started to expand the Tiberius team, including bringing on board Baynes as chief strategy officer in 2023. Baynes had first traveled to Ukraine around a decade ago to investigate how local startup Ring, now owned by Amazon, had outdone Nest, which he’d been working on and eventually sold to Google. news.article_content_zh:
斯蒂尔伯格与谷歌校友、苹果前高管安迪·贝恩斯一起表示，他们正在努力打破硅谷式的俄罗斯-乌克兰战争“僵局”。他们相信，他们快速构建和迭代技术的经验可以帮助西方武器制造与战场上的快速创新周期保持一致，并击败贝恩斯所描述的战争已经成为的“消耗性猫鼠技术游戏”。

斯蒂尔伯格来自加利福尼亚州纽波特比奇，2022 年初，他将数百名乌克兰难民收容到自己的法国城堡中后，他就开始渴望在战场上“有所作为”。他说，每当家乡的丈夫、父亲或儿子收到坏消息时，他都会因悲伤而“心碎”。 “我相信我真的可以改变这场战争以及每场战争的结果，”斯蒂尔伯格告诉《连线》杂志。 “我并不是说这纯粹是无私的，”他补充道。 “当然，我们会通过这样做赚钱。”

本周，他们的公司 Tiberius Aerospace 表示，已获得 8500 万美元的 A 轮融资，由欧洲技术投资公司 Lakestar 和 Rochefort Asset Management（一家获得美国国防部许可的专注于国家安全的投资公司）牵头。乌克兰风险投资公司UA1也是投资者。

Tiberius 最初是 Steelberg 的私人研究实验室，成立于 2021 年，雇佣了来自法国、英国和美国的人员，对从无人机、电动垂直起飞飞机到量子计算等一系列技术的前沿想法进行实验。入侵后，他让实验室的人工智能和航空航天工程师转向编写代码和构建电子表格，以客观地分析战争的许多因素并计算出什么可以推动局势发展。他们创建的人工智能模型很快就排除了建立更好的防御技术的可能性，因为这只会加剧僵局。

斯蒂尔伯格的目标缩小到制造进攻性武器，他开发了几个指标来对不同系统的杀伤力（包括成本效益）进行数值分析，并使用人工智能引擎模拟不同条件下的武器，并确定什么会扰乱市场。它建议，不要再制造一架无人机，而应该制造射程更远的火炮。由此产生的系统称为“Sceptre”，可以从 155 毫米榴弹炮发射，这是捐赠给乌克兰的最常见的火炮武器。他们声称，除了比目前可用的弹药飞行得更远之外，它们还可以达到超出干扰范围的超音速和高度。

英国国防智库皇家联合军种研究所副研究员萨姆·克兰尼-埃文斯告诉《连线》杂志，让乌克兰的火炮拥有更大的射程非常重要，因为这将使乌克兰炮手能够在俄罗斯无人机攻击范围之外进行作战。他说，155 毫米炮弹“可能对一群车辆或步兵造成巨大伤害”。 “任何能够帮助乌克兰扩大榴弹炮射程并使其重新投入战斗的技术都将是有价值的。”

凭借在 AI 帮助下设计的原型，Steelberg 还开始扩大 Tiberius 团队，包括在 2023 年任命 Baynes 担任首席战略官。Baynes 大约十年前首次前往乌克兰，调查当地初创公司 Ring（现为亚马逊旗下）如何超越他一直在开发并最终出售给谷歌的 Nest。他爱上了基辅雄心勃勃的软件工程师和蓬勃发展的科技场景——负责开发全球成功的科技工具，例如 Grammarly 和 Snapchat 的面部滤镜。 2016年，他收购了当地一家生命科学科技公司，旨在通过自动化临床试验和改进蛋白质模型来加速下一代药物的开发。 “吸引我来到基辅的是工程界的渴望和雄心，”他告诉《连线》杂志。 “很难不被它极大地吸引，并看看它是否可以应用于真正关键的任务问题集，例如癌症药物或加速生命科学公司的临床试验。”

俄罗斯入侵后，贝恩斯在布达佩斯驻扎了大约六个月，帮助疏散妇女和儿童以及将设备运送到该国的后勤工作。他请求他的全球网络帮助为难民寻找医疗设备、车辆和住宿，这让他重新与斯蒂尔伯格取得了联系。贝恩斯认为，西方对入侵的反应“不够”，乌克兰需要更好的进攻能力来击退俄罗斯军队。

4 月，Tiberius 宣布首次从北约标准 155 毫米榴弹炮成功发射了一枚权杖炮弹。该公司目前正在与美国陆军合作完善该系统，并宣布与英国合作伙伴签订价值 5 亿美元的技术合作合同，以制造、许可和分销该弹药。它还正在开发一种导弹，预计明年将开始产生收入。

Tiberius 将其最初构建的人工智能系统转变为一款名为 GRAIL（杀伤力生成实时人工智能）的产品。斯蒂尔伯格表示，他对此“最兴奋”。他希望该平台能够通过分散制造来实现 Tiberius 许可的武器设计的持续升级。斯蒂尔伯格表示，除了自动化供应链管理和合规性之外，该软件还可以模拟在一系列环境和天气条件下（例如北极半岛）针对不同目标的武器。除了开源数据外，该团队还试图获取来自世界各地（包括乌克兰）的热门实时战斗数据。我们的想法是，这一切都使用户能够更快地测试、迭代和设计用于特定用途的武器。

“在人工智能、设计和开发越来越快的世界里，西方或盟国集团拥有不可否认的优势是什么？”贝恩斯问道。 “如果你能将英国、法国、德国、北欧国家和美国的所有闲置产能和精密制造武器化，”他说，“那是我们今天的对手永远无法比拟的。”向史蒂夫·乔布斯汇报了四年的贝恩斯继续说道，提比略的目标是通过复制“苹果模式”来实现这一目标。他表示，将制造业务外包给许多第三方分包商可以加速开发和部署，并在和平时期将昂贵的生产成本从 Tiberius 的资产负债表中扣除。

“我们正在采取硅谷的方法，”斯蒂尔伯格说。 “当你遇到一个大的、棘手的、棘手的问题时，你不仅要跨越它，而且要转身，建造一座桥梁——显然，这是一座收费桥...

celebrity.full_text_en:
Teammate on Fable 5.2 made HADAL, a dive into the Mariana Trench you can play in a browser tab at https://t.co/wgZHPEaeRy. You start as a scuba diver on a sunlit reef, board a submarine, and work your way down past shipwrecks, a whale fall and other things to Challenger Deep, scanning 18 discoveries as you go.

Everything on screen is code. Teammate wrote the WebGPU renderer itself, with no game engine and no Three.js, and generated the terrain, kelp, creatures, submarine and sound without a single imported model, texture or audio file. It all fits in one 373 KB HTML file.

36,000 Perplexity credits on Ultra Effort (Fable 5.2 High as orchestrator).

celebrity.title_zh:
突发新闻：#BNY 和@Microsoft 使用#AI 代理完成了行业首个美国国库券试点贸易谈判。

该交易是根据纽约银行的代理谈判协议（ANP）进行的，这是一个值得信赖的框架，跨组织的授权代理在确定性规则和护栏的指导下安全、透明地进行谈判
celebrity.full_text_en:
BREAKING: #BNY and @Microsoft complete industry-first pilot trade negotiation of U.S. Treasury bill using #AI agents.

The trade was conducted under BNY's Agentic Negotiation Protocol (ANP) — a trusted framework where authorized agents across organizations negotiate securely and transparently, guided by deterministic rules and guardrails. Human traders remain in the loop and retain the final decision, and all trades are booked through existing systems and controls.

This milestone demonstrates how AI #agents can be deployed responsibly in institutional markets.

celebrity.full_text_en:
An AI agent saying “I can help with research” doesn’t tell me enough to hire it.

Research what, exactly?

Can it compare protocols, collect onchain data, identify risks, or produce a report with verifiable sources?

There’s a big difference between listing a capability and presenting a service someone can confidently pay for.

That’s one part of the agent economy I’m interested in exploring through @termix_ai and https://t.co/VQiubSQwfg

A useful agent service listing should make a few things clear:

• The problem it solves: what can someone actually hire this agent to do?

• The deliverable: what will the client receive at the end?

• The scope: what is included, and what isn’t?

• The expectations: what does a successful result look like?

This matters because discovery is only the beginning.

An agent might have impressive capabilities, but if a potential client cannot understand the service or what they will receive, turning that discovery into a real job becomes difficult.

With https://t.co/VQiubSQwfg, agents can create service listings that people can discover and purchase.

I like looking at this from the client’s side too. Before hiring an agent, I want to know what I’m buying, not just how intelligent its description sounds.

The agent economy will need capable agents, yes. But it will also need agents that know how to present their work as a clear, useful service.

That’s how skills start becoming commerce.
celebrity.full_text_zh:
人工智能代理说“我可以帮助研究”并没有告诉我足够的信息来雇用它。

到底研究什么？

它可以比较协议、收集链上数据、识别风险或生成来源可验证的报告吗？

列出一项功能和提供一项人们可以放心付费的服务之间存在很大差异。

这是我有兴趣通过 @termix_ai 和 探索代理经济的一部分

有用的代理服务列表应该明确以下几点：

• 它解决的问题：有人可以实际雇用该代理来做什么？

• 可交付成果：客户最终会收到什么？

• 范围：包括什么，不包括什么？

• 期望：成功的结果是什么样的？

这很重要，因为发现仅仅是开始。

代理可能拥有令人印象深刻的能力，但如果潜在客户无法理解服务或他们将收到什么，那么将这种发现转化为真正的工作就会变得困难。

通过 ，代理商可以创建人们可以发现和购买的服务列表。

我也喜欢从客户的角度来看这个问题。在聘请代理商之前，我想知道我要买什么，而不仅仅是它的描述听起来有多聪明。

是的，代理经济需要有能力的代理。但它也需要代理知道如何将他们的工作呈现为清晰、有用的服务。

这就是技能开始成为商业的方式。

celebrity.full_text_en:
was reading @Acurast's new post about the Microsoft outage on November 12, and one part got me thinking.

Outlook, Teams and Copilot were all affected by the same outage. Different services, but they still depended on the same company's infrastructure.

Acurast points out something interesting here.

Instead of running everything in one cloud, developers can spread their workloads across phones in different countries. If one phone goes offline, other phones running the same workload can keep working.

Their network now has over 360,000 phones across 175+ countries, according to the latest blog.

But I think there's an important difference.

Acurast can't magically fix Outlook when Microsoft's servers go down. And an AI agent that needs Outlook's API would still have problems.

What it can do is help keep independent tasks running, like monitoring services or sending alerts through another system.

I'd actually like to see Acurast test this in public. Take one Processor offline while a real application is running and show how the network handles it.

That would tell us more about reliability than just counting connected phones.
celebrity.full_text_zh:
11 月 12 日，我正在阅读 @Acurast 关于 Microsoft 宕机事件的新帖子，其中一个内容引起了我的思考。

Outlook、Teams 和 Copilot 均受到同一故障的影响。不同的服务，但它们仍然依赖于同一家公司的基础设施。

阿库拉斯特在这里指出了一些有趣的事情。

开发人员可以将工作负载分散到不同国家/地区的手机上，而不是在一个云中运行所有内容。如果一部电话离线，运行相同工作负载的其他电话可以继续工作。

根据最新博客，他们的网络目前在 175 多个国家/地区拥有超过 360,000 部电话。

但我认为有一个重要的区别。

当 Microsoft 的服务器出现故障时，Acurast 无法神奇地修复 Outlook。而需要 Outlook API 的 AI 代理仍然会遇到问题。

它可以做的是帮助保持独立任务的运行，例如监控服务或通过另一个系统发送警报。

我实际上希望看到 Acurast 公开测试这一点。在实际应用程序运行时使一个处理器离线并显示网络如何处理它。

这将告诉我们更多关于可靠性的信息，而不仅仅是计算连接的电话。

celebrity.full_text_en:
“Delivered” can start an argument as easily as end one.

Imagine an agent ordering steel for a project. The shipment arrives. The buyer disputes whether it meets the specification.

Both agents have a reason to say they’re right. Who settles it?

That’s the lens I’m using for @GenLayer move to the @arbitrum stack.

The GenLayer Chain moved from ZK Stack to Nitro. It hosts the consensus contracts that track who judges a case, their votes, appeals and the final outcome.

The method of judgment stays the same. Validators running different AI models reach agreement through Optimistic Democracy. Intelligent contracts still execute in GenVM on validator nodes.

My take: the rules for resolving a disagreement should survive a change in the infrastructure recording it. GenLayer preserved that boundary while moving its chain to a stack with years of production use.

For anyone building agents that spend money, here’s a question worth answering before the first purchase:

What would your agent need to see before accepting “job done”?
celebrity.full_text_zh:

两位经纪人都有理由说他们是对的。谁来解决？

这就是我用于将 @GenLayer 迁移到 @arbitrum 堆栈的镜头。

GenLayer 链从 ZK Stack 迁移到 Nitro。它托管共识合约，跟踪案件的法官、他们的投票、上诉和最终结果。

判断方法保持不变。运行不同人工智能模型的验证者通过乐观民主达成一致。智能合约仍在验证器节点上的 GenVM 中执行。

我的看法是：解决分歧的规则应该在记录分歧的基础设施发生变化后继续存在。 GenLayer 保留了这一边界，同时将其链转移到具有多年生产使用的堆栈中。

对于任何花钱的建筑代理商来说，在第一次购买之前，有一个值得回答的问题：

在接受“工作完成”之前，您的代理人需要看到什么？

celebrity.full_text_en:
A court does not run its own power grid. GenLayer, the adjudication layer for AI agents, follows a similar split.

Its chain moved to Arbitrum Nitro, the same software behind the chain Robinhood launched in July.

That chain is operated with Conduit, a company whose whole business is running chains, with more than 60 mainnets on its platform. The GenLayer team keeps its hands on the protocol.

I like that division of labour. Optimistic Democracy, GenVM and intelligent contracts are where GenLayer's judgment lives, and the move leaves them as they were. Validators keep the same role, and their nodes now connect to the new chain.

The next phase of the Bradbury testnet went live the same day. The work with ZKsync continues on Prividium and enterprise, while the public network is the part that moved.

@GenLayer chose a stack that others already run on, and @arbitrum is where many of the builders it wants to work with already are.

Would you rather a protocol team run its own chain, or leave that part to specialists?
celebrity.full_text_zh:
法院不运营自己的电网。 GenLayer 是人工智能代理的裁决层，也遵循类似的划分。

它的链转移到 Arbitrum Nitro，这与 7 月份推出的 Robinhood 链背后的软件相同。

该链由 Conduit 运营，该公司的全部业务都是运营链，其平台上有 60 多个主网。 GenLayer 团队负责掌握该协议。

我喜欢这种分工。乐观民主、GenVM 和智能合约是 GenLayer 的判断所在，而此举让它们保持原样。验证者保持相同的角色，他们的节点现在连接到新链。

布拉德伯里测试网的下一阶段于同一天上线。 ZKsync 的工作在 Prividium 和企业上继续进行，而公共网络是移动的部分。

@GenLayer 选择了其他人已经运行的堆栈，而 @arbitrum 是它想要使用的许多构建器已经所在的位置。

您希望协议团队运行自己的链，还是将该部分留给专家？

celebrity.title_zh:
👻 YO-KAI WATCH 4++ 重新编译为 PC 带来了 4K、超宽、高 FPS 和原生 Linux 支持！ 🎮🔥

开发商 ILFforever 正在通过静态重新编译将 Level-5 的 Nintendo Switch 动作 RP
celebrity.full_text_en:
👻 YO-KAI WATCH 4++ RECOMPILATION brings 4K, ultrawide, high FPS and native Linux support to PC! 🎮🔥

Developer ILFforever is bringing Level-5's Nintendo Switch action RPG to Windows and Linux through static recompilation, translating the original ARM64 game code into a native PC application with a Vulkan graphics renderer!

🔥 FEATURES:

✅ NATIVE WINDOWS & LINUX! Including a Linux AppImage launcher — no Switch emulator required!

✅ 4K & ULTRAWIDE! Supports 1080p, 1440p, 4K and 21:9/32:9 aspect ratios!

✅ HIGH FRAME RATES! 30, 60, 120, 144 FPS and uncapped options!

✅ DLSS & FSR! Upscaling and frame generation for smoother presentation, with platform-specific support!

✅ ENHANCED GRAPHICS! PCSS soft shadows, improved anti-aliasing, TAA, SMAA and sharper textures!

✅ MOD SUPPORT! Includes compatibility with the fan-made English translation patch!

✅ MODERN CONTROLS! Keyboard, mouse, Xbox, PlayStation and Joy-Con controllers, with configurable bindings and vibration!

✅ DEDICATED LAUNCHER! Import your own game files, build the PC version, manage updates, saves, DLC and mods!

🔥 BETA v1.5.0 — PLAYABLE BUT UNFINISHED!

The opening, several locations and late-game battles have been tested. However, most of the story remains unverified, so crashes and missing graphical effects are possible.

💿 Requires your own Yo-kai Watch 4++ Nintendo Switch game files, updated to version 2.2.0.

🛠️ Developed by ILFforever, with extensive AI-assisted programming using Claude Code.

⭐ Star the GitHub repository and support continued development!

💻 PROJECT & DOWNLOADS:

🔗https://t.co/l7Td19CWSA

🌐 Discover more PC ports, recompilations and fan projects:

🔗https://t.co/9gMW2oiuvM

👻 YO-KAI WATCH 4++ 重新编译为 PC 带来了 4K、超宽、高 FPS 和原生 Linux 支持！ 🎮🔥

开发商 ILFforever 正在通过静态重新编译将 Level-5 的 Nintendo Switch 动作 RPG 引入 Windows 和 Linux，将原始 ARM64 游戏代码转换为带有 Vulkan 图形渲染器的本机 PC 应用程序！

🔥 特点：

✅ 本机 WINDOWS 和 LINUX！包括 Linux AppImage 启动器 - 无需 Switch 模拟器！

✅ 4K 和超宽！支持 1080p、1440p、4K 和 21:9/32:9 宽高比！

✅ 高帧率！ 30、60、120、144 FPS 和无上限选项！

✅ DLSS 和 FSR！升级和帧生成可实现更流畅的演示，并提供特定于平台的支持！

✅ 增强的图形！ PCSS 柔和阴影、改进的抗锯齿、TAA、SMAA 和更清晰的纹理！

✅ 模组支持！包括与粉丝制作的英文翻译补丁的兼容性！

✅ 现代控制！键盘、鼠标、Xbox、PlayStation 和 Joy-Con 控制器，具有可配置的绑定和振动！

✅ 专用发射器！导入您自己的游戏文件、构建 PC 版本、管理更新、保存、DLC 和模组！

🔥 BETA v1.5.0 — 可玩但未完成！

开局、多个地点和游戏后期的战斗都经过了测试。然而，故事的大部分内容仍未得到验证，因此可能会出现崩溃和图形效果缺失的情况。

💿 需要您自己的 Yo-kai Watch 4++ Nintendo Switch 游戏文件，已更新至版本 2.2.0。

🛠️ 由 ILFforever 开发，使用 Claude Code 进行广泛的人工智能辅助编程。

prompts.scenario: 💻 编程研发 / 自动化规范
prompts.takeaway_zh: 杜绝 AI 盲目重构全量文件、使用已弃用 API 或编造虚假第三方依赖包，强制执行防御性编程与自动化单测补全。
prompts.takeaway_en: Prevents AI from hallucinating npm packages, breaking documentation, or re-writing entire files. Enforces defensive coding and unit tests.
prompts.code_snippet:
# Cursor & Windsurf Project Rules (.cursorrules)

## 1. Documentation & Code Integrity
- Maintain documentation integrity: Never strip or alter unrelated existing docstrings and comments.
- Preserving context: When modifying a function, preserve surrounding logic and existing edge-case handlers.
- Targeted replacements: Always make minimal surgical edits instead of replacing entire file contents.

## 2. Dependency & API Safety
- Strictly forbid hallucinating npm/pip packages. Only import dependencies already declared in package.json / requirements.txt.
- Verify API signatures before calling external methods. Prefer standard library solutions where feasible.

## 3. Architecture & Type Safety
- Enforce strict TypeScript / Python typing. Avoid `any` types; prefer discriminated unions and explicit return types.
- Defensive coding: Always validate external inputs and handle potential null/undefined values gracefully.

## 4. Testing & Verification Gate
- Every new core feature or bugfix must be accompanied by corresponding unit tests.
- Never declare a task complete without executing lint checks and unit tests in terminal.
prompts.usage_guide_zh: 将以上配置代码复制并保存到项目根目录下的 `.cursorrules` 文件中，Cursor 与 Windsurf 在每次生成代码和执行 Agent 任务时均会自动以此规范为最高准则约束输出。
prompts.usage_guide_en: Copy and save the above rules into `.cursorrules` in your project root directory. Cursor & Windsurf will automatically enforce these guidelines during agent coding.

请作为普林斯顿高等研究院的理论数学与计算机科学家，为以下命题提供绝对严格的形式化证明：
【推理原则】：
1. 在得出任何推论前，强制在内部思考中构建至少 2 个极端反例（Counter-examples）尝试推翻自身结论；
2. 若存在任何定义域边界或除零/无穷/退化奇异点，必须显式讨论其收敛性与连续性；
3. 证明步骤编号必须形成严格的依赖拓扑图，禁止循环论证。

【待证明命题】：
[输入你的算法正确性证明或数学猜想]

2. Explicitly evaluate singular points, degenerate cases, and asymptotic boundaries for convergence;
3. Steps must form a directed acyclic graph of formal lemmas without circular logic.

[THEOREM / CONJECTURE]:
[Input your algorithm proof or mathematical hypothesis here]

prompts.prompt_content_zh:
你是一名专攻短视频微短剧（抖音/Kuaishou/Reels）的爆款编剧，精通“情绪过山车”与手机竖屏视听语言。

请根据以下设定创作一集 45~60 秒的短剧分镜剧本：
- 主角：{{主角身份}}
- 对手：{{反派身份}}
- 核心反转：{{核心反转}}

结构要求：
1. 【0-3秒冷开钩子】：第一帧必须有视觉颠覆或动作冲突（{{第1秒颠覆钩子}}），直接打破常规，禁止废话铺垫；
2. 【4-25秒情绪积压】：正反打对峙台词（Shot-Reverse-Shot），将观众被压抑的情绪推向临界点；
3. 【26-40秒逆转打脸】：主角亮出关键底牌或反杀动作，情绪瞬间宣泄；
4. 【40-50秒卡点断章】：以特写镜头加悬念台词戛然而止，促使用户立即滑向下一集。

输出格式必须包含：镜头号、景别（特写/中景/全景）、机位运动、画面描写、对白与音效提示。

sample_output.title: 实战剧本样章：《辞职信上的签名》

音效：沉闷震耳的巨响【DUANG】。
主角（冷冽）："林总，这份千万项目的承揽协议，我拒绝签字。"

prompts.prompt_content_zh:
你是一名麦肯锡级别的高级商业数据分析师，精通结构化因果归因与杜邦拆解分析。

针对我提供的 {{业务指标}} 数据，其近期出现 {{异常表现}}，请按以下框架深度剖析：
1. 【指标公式拆解】：将该指标拆分为 3~4 个下级核心因子（如转化率、客单价、复购周期），指出哪个因子波动贡献率最大；
2. 【多维下钻 (Drill-down)】：从 {{维度拆解}}（如渠道、地域、品类、新老客）分析异常聚集点；
3. 【可执行建议】：摒弃假大空的套话，给出接下来 48 小时内的 3 个立竿见影的动作与 1 个监控预警公式。
prompts.prompt_content_en: You are a senior business intelligence analyst. Dissect the metric anomaly into component drivers, perform multi-dimensional drill-down, and deliver prioritized, actionable remediation steps.

sample_output.title: 归因分析报告样本：Q3 付费转化率环比下跌 14.2%
sample_output.content:

viral_posts.full_text_en:
An AI agent saying “I can help with research” doesn’t tell me enough to hire it.

Research what, exactly?

Can it compare protocols, collect onchain data, identify risks, or produce a report with verifiable sources?

There’s a big difference between listing a capability and presenting a service someone can confidently pay for.

That’s one part of the agent economy I’m interested in exploring through @termix_ai and https://t.co/VQiubSQwfg

A useful agent service listing should make a few things clear:

• The problem it solves: what can someone actually hire this agent to do?

• The deliverable: what will the client receive at the end?

• The scope: what is included, and what isn’t?

• The expectations: what does a successful result look like?

This matters because discovery is only the beginning.

An agent might have impressive capabilities, but if a potential client cannot understand the service or what they will receive, turning that discovery into a real job becomes difficult.

With https://t.co/VQiubSQwfg, agents can create service listings that people can discover and purchase.

I like looking at this from the client’s side too. Before hiring an agent, I want to know what I’m buying, not just how intelligent its description sounds.

The agent economy will need capable agents, yes. But it will also need agents that know how to present their work as a clear, useful service.

That’s how skills start becoming commerce.
viral_posts.full_text_zh:
人工智能代理说“我可以帮助研究”并没有告诉我足够的信息来雇用它。

到底研究什么？

它可以比较协议、收集链上数据、识别风险或生成来源可验证的报告吗？

列出一项功能和提供一项人们可以放心付费的服务之间存在很大差异。

这是我有兴趣通过 @termix_ai 和 探索代理经济的一部分

有用的代理服务列表应该明确以下几点：

• 它解决的问题：有人可以实际雇用该代理来做什么？

• 可交付成果：客户最终会收到什么？

• 范围：包括什么，不包括什么？

• 期望：成功的结果是什么样的？

这很重要，因为发现仅仅是开始。

代理可能拥有令人印象深刻的能力，但如果潜在客户无法理解服务或他们将收到什么，那么将这种发现转化为真正的工作就会变得困难。

通过 ，代理商可以创建人们可以发现和购买的服务列表。

我也喜欢从客户的角度来看这个问题。在聘请代理商之前，我想知道我要买什么，而不仅仅是它的描述听起来有多聪明。

是的，代理经济需要有能力的代理。但它也需要代理知道如何将他们的工作呈现为清晰、有用的服务。

这就是技能开始成为商业的方式。

viral_posts.title_zh:

Outlook、Teams 和 Copilot 均受到同一故障的影响。不同的服务，但它们仍然依赖于同一家公司的基础
viral_posts.full_text_en:
was reading @Acurast's new post about the Microsoft outage on November 12, and one part got me thinking.

Outlook, Teams and Copilot were all affected by the same outage. Different services, but they still depended on the same company's infrastructure.

Acurast points out something interesting here.

Instead of running everything in one cloud, developers can spread their workloads across phones in different countries. If one phone goes offline, other phones running the same workload can keep working.

Their network now has over 360,000 phones across 175+ countries, according to the latest blog.

But I think there's an important difference.

Acurast can't magically fix Outlook when Microsoft's servers go down. And an AI agent that needs Outlook's API would still have problems.

What it can do is help keep independent tasks running, like monitoring services or sending alerts through another system.

I'd actually like to see Acurast test this in public. Take one Processor offline while a real application is running and show how the network handles it.

That would tell us more about reliability than just counting connected phones.
viral_posts.full_text_zh:
11 月 12 日，我正在阅读 @Acurast 关于 Microsoft 宕机事件的新帖子，其中一个内容引起了我的思考。

Outlook、Teams 和 Copilot 均受到同一故障的影响。不同的服务，但它们仍然依赖于同一家公司的基础设施。

阿库拉斯特在这里指出了一些有趣的事情。

开发人员可以将工作负载分散到不同国家/地区的手机上，而不是在一个云中运行所有内容。如果一部电话离线，运行相同工作负载的其他电话可以继续工作。

根据最新博客，他们的网络目前在 175 多个国家/地区拥有超过 360,000 部电话。

但我认为有一个重要的区别。

当 Microsoft 的服务器出现故障时，Acurast 无法神奇地修复 Outlook。而需要 Outlook API 的 AI 代理仍然会遇到问题。

它可以做的是帮助保持独立任务的运行，例如监控服务或通过另一个系统发送警报。

我实际上希望看到 Acurast 公开测试这一点。在实际应用程序运行时使一个处理器离线并显示网络如何处理它。

这将告诉我们更多关于可靠性的信息，而不仅仅是计算连接的电话。

viral_posts.full_text_en:
“Delivered” can start an argument as easily as end one.

Imagine an agent ordering steel for a project. The shipment arrives. The buyer disputes whether it meets the specification.

Both agents have a reason to say they’re right. Who settles it?

That’s the lens I’m using for @GenLayer move to the @arbitrum stack.

The GenLayer Chain moved from ZK Stack to Nitro. It hosts the consensus contracts that track who judges a case, their votes, appeals and the final outcome.

The method of judgment stays the same. Validators running different AI models reach agreement through Optimistic Democracy. Intelligent contracts still execute in GenVM on validator nodes.

My take: the rules for resolving a disagreement should survive a change in the infrastructure recording it. GenLayer preserved that boundary while moving its chain to a stack with years of production use.

For anyone building agents that spend money, here’s a question worth answering before the first purchase:

What would your agent need to see before accepting “job done”?
viral_posts.full_text_zh:
“交付”可以像结束争论一样轻松地开始一场争论。

想象一下一个代理商为一个项目订购钢材。货物到达。买方对是否符合规格提出异议。

两位经纪人都有理由说他们是对的。谁来解决？

这就是我用于将 @GenLayer 迁移到 @arbitrum 堆栈的镜头。

GenLayer 链从 ZK Stack 迁移到 Nitro。它托管共识合约，跟踪案件的法官、他们的投票、上诉和最终结果。

判断方法保持不变。运行不同人工智能模型的验证者通过乐观民主达成一致。智能合约仍在验证器节点上的 GenVM 中执行。

我的看法是：解决分歧的规则应该在记录分歧的基础设施发生变化后继续存在。 GenLayer 保留了这一边界，同时将其链转移到具有多年生产使用的堆栈中。

对于任何花钱的建筑代理商来说，在第一次购买之前，有一个值得回答的问题：

在接受“工作完成”之前，您的代理人需要看到什么？

That frustration became @GenLayer.
